gap: No result ChatGPT got states that no named reviewer or lab has published bench measurements (trip voltage, reconnect time, current-reading accuracy) for the Hughes Power Watchdog Gen II or the Kasa plugs; the only independent figures are Mike Sokol's general EMS behaviour (shuts off about 8 to 180 s after voltage goes above about 128 V or below about 105 V; RVelectricity, 12 Oct 2026), which matches the maker's 104 V / 132 V cutoffs.
standout_why: I compared against rvupgradestore.com PWD30EPOW (cited), which already lists 2,300 J, a 104 V low cutoff and a 132 V high cutoff. hughesautoformers.com/power-watchdog-2nd-gen and /product/pwd30-epo (cited) now 301-redirect to powerwatchdog.com, whose pages failed to load (self-signed certificate) and could not be read. None of the rival pages has a third-party measurement, but I found none to add either. Sokol's piece gives only generic EMS timing and thresholds, and Getaway Couple only repeats spec joule ratings.
decides: It doesn't change the pick. No named measurement separates the Power Watchdog Gen II from Progressive Industries or Southwire on protection, so a page has to compare them on maker specs (cutoffs, joules, Wi-Fi app, EPO shutoff) and price. Sokol's general EMS description supports ChatGPT's advice to put an EMS-type 30/50 A unit at the pedestal and keep 15 A plugs for single appliances. A useful price fact: rvupgradestore.com showed the PWD30EPOW on sale at $279.99 on 2026-11-10, against the $379.99 list price ChatGPT quoted.

unsourced: A bench or lab measurement by a named reviewer of the Power Watchdog Gen II's actual trip voltage, reconnect delay (maker says 90 s) or app voltage/current accuracy: searched RVelectricity (Mike Sokol) Substack, rvtravel.com (403), Getaway Couple, and RV review roundups; Sokol says only that he did 'casual testing' and signed an NDA, with no brand figures.
Brand-specific open-ground trigger thresholds: Sokol's 'Open Ground Testing' post (2024-05-13) says they differ by brand but gives no per-brand figures.
Measured trip points for Progressive Industries EMS-PT30X or Southwire Surge Guard from a named tester: only forum anecdotes found.

Measured energy-monitoring accuracy and standby draw for the Kasa EP25 / EP40A by a named reviewer: Wirecutter and PCMag were not fetchable, TechGearLab didn't measure them, and the blog claims of '~2%' had no traceable method.

Hughes/Power Watchdog maker pages (powerwatchdog.com/surge-protectors, /shop): would not load (self-signed certificate chain), so I couldn't confirm maker specs or prices there; the cited hughesautoformers.com URLs now 301-redirect to powerwatchdog.com.
